Hon'ble Karunesh Singh Pawar,J.
Heard learned counsel for applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate for State.

The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to F.I.R. No.
376/2022, under Sections 419/420/506 IPC, P.S. Kotwali Dehat, District Gonda.
Notices to respondent no. 2 are dispensed in view of the proposed order.

entities.text: Abhishek Kumar Singh @ Ajju vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 Learned A.G.A. for the respondent State has raised preliminary objection that the offences are punishable up to seven years, therefore, it cannot be presumed that there is any apprehension of arrest of the applicant.

In view of law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of "Satender Kumar Antil versus Central Bureau of Investigation and another, Special Leave to Appeal (Cri)
No.5191 of 2021 the applicant can very well appear and surrender before the trial court and shall be enlarged on bail without being taken into custody.

entities.text:
Satender Kumar Antil versus Central Bureau of Investigation and another, Special Leave to Appeal (Cri)
No.5191 of 2021
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The anticipatory bail is not maintainable as there is no apprehension of arrest.

In view of submissions made by the learned A.G.A. so also considering the law laid down in the case of Satender Kumar Antil, I am not inclined to entertain the anticipatory bail application, hence, the application is rejected.

However, liberty is granted to the applicant to file a regular bail application before the learned trial court, which, if filed within a period of 15 days, shall be considered and decided strictly in view of the law laid down by Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
